sections.skill: Notice requirements that cannot all be met

questions.domain: Foundation 4: Asking for what you need
questions.prompt: Which request contains a conflict?

choices.text: "Explain the steps for a 10-year-old reader."
"Explain every step in full detail in 20 words."
"Explain the steps for beginners, in plain words."
"Explain the steps as a numbered list."

questions.correct_answer: "Explain every step in full detail in 20 words."
questions.intro: Some requests contain CONFLICTING REQUIREMENTS: rules that cannot all be met at once. "Explain the history of the internet in full detail in 50 words" is one; "make it formal and very casual" is another. A tool usually does not stop to ask. It quietly breaks one rule, blends both badly, or claims success anyway. Watch for conflicts in length versus detail, tone versus audience, and speed versus completeness. When you notice one, decide which requirement matters more, or how to split the job, before continuing, for example two versions or a short summary plus a longer appendix.
questions.feedback: Full detail and 20 words cannot both be met.

sections.skill: Compare conflicting rules with a packing list

questions.domain: Foundation 4: Asking for what you need
questions.prompt: What is the conflict in the packing example?

choices.text: A small bag versus a bright blue bag
Everything you need versus one small bag
Morning versus evening
Shoes versus socks

questions.correct_answer: Everything you need versus one small bag
questions.intro: Imagine packing for a trip with two rules: "Bring everything you might need" and "Use only one small backpack." You cannot follow both. If you do not decide, you might stuff the bag until it breaks, or leave behind something important without noticing. A sensible traveler decides which rule wins ("the small bag is required, so bring only essentials") or changes the plan ("take a second bag"). Conflicting requirements in a request work the same way.
questions.feedback: The two rules cannot both be met.

questions.domain: Foundation 4: Asking for what you need
questions.prompt: Earlier in a chat you said "always under 100 words." Now you ask for every detail of a long report. What might happen?

choices.text: The tool will refuse all future requests
The old rule clashes with the new request
The old rule disappears automatically
The report will be summarized perfectly

questions.correct_answer: The old rule clashes with the new request
questions.intro: Conflicts are not always visible in the request itself. A rule from earlier in a conversation ("always under 100 words") can clash with a new request ("include every detail from this 20-page report"). A supplied document can conflict with your instructions, such as a template with five sections when you asked for three. When results look strange, look for an older or hidden rule. Ask the tool to point out any conflicting requirements before it starts, and resolve them yourself instead of letting it choose.
questions.feedback: Older rules can conflict with new ones.
